subject: DBMS
title: Discover Primary & Foreign Keys
description: Discover how database keys identify rows and connect related tables.

mission.title: Trace a Table Relationship
mission.description: Follow a payment's foreign key to the student row identified by a primary key.

actions.label: Trace it to the Students table

quiz.question: Payments.STUDENT_ID contains 102. Students.ID = 102 belongs to Mary. Who made that payment?

discovery.title: Keys Connect Records
discovery.summary: A foreign key stores a value that references a primary key in another table, allowing related records to be connected.

sections.title: What is a primary key?
sections.content: A primary key is a column whose value identifies one specific row in a table.

sections.title: Unique rows
sections.content: Primary-key values must be unique, so two different students cannot both have ID 102.

sections.title: What is a foreign key?
sections.content: A foreign key is a value in one table that refers to a primary-key value in another table.

sections.title: Creating relationships
sections.content: Foreign keys connect related records without repeating all of the student information in every payment row.

sections.title: One-to-many relationships
sections.content: One student can be connected to many payment rows, but each payment row points to one student.

sections.title: Why databases use keys
sections.content: Keys keep data organized, make records easier to find, and help tables stay connected correctly.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a student ID card
alternate_explanations.content: A student ID is a unique label for one student. A payment record can write that ID down instead of copying the student's whole name.

alternate_explanations.title: Trace payment P001
alternate_explanations.content: Payment P001 stores STUDENT_ID 102. Follow 102 to Students.ID 102, which identifies Mary. The foreign key leads to the matching primary-key row.

introduction.title: Meet Database Keys
introduction.content: Databases use keys so they can identify one record exactly and connect records in different tables without copying all the details.
points: A primary key uniquely identifies one row.
A foreign key stores a matching value from another table.
You will trace a payment back to the student it belongs to.

worked_example.title: Trace one payment
worked_example.content: A foreign-key value is a clue that points to one matching primary-key row.

steps.explanation: P001 stores 102 in its STUDENT_ID column. That is the foreign key to follow.
Students.ID is a primary key, so exactly one student has ID 102.
The matching values connect this payment record to Mary.

worked_example.conclusion: The foreign key does not need to repeat Mary's name; its matching ID creates the relationship.

next.title: Trace the highlighted relationship.
next.content: Use TRACE RELATION to follow a foreign-key value across the two tables.

action_explanations.find-foreign-key: STUDENT_ID is the foreign-key value stored in the payment row; it is the link to follow.
action_explanations.trace-to-students: The line follows the same number from PAYMENTS.STUDENT_ID to STUDENTS.ID.
action_explanations.match-primary-key: A primary key is unique, so matching 102 identifies only one Students row.
action_explanations.identify-student: The row with ID 102 belongs to Mary, so Mary made this payment.
action_explanations.complete-another-relationship: Another payment can use the same kind of ID match to connect to its student.

challenge.title: Relationship Challenge
challenge.start_message: Trace a payment to its student by following the key values rather than guessing from the names.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep tracing payments to see the same relationship rule work again.

phases.title: Identify the first student
phases.instruction: Follow P001's STUDENT_ID until you can name the matching student.

target.label: Goal
target.description: Match PAYMENTS.STUDENT_ID 102 with STUDENTS.ID 102 and identify Mary.

phases.feedback: Start at the payment's STUDENT_ID, then look for the same value in the Students primary-key column.

phases.title: Trace another payment
phases.instruction: Use the same key-matching idea for the next payment relationship.

target.label: Goal
target.description: Show that a different STUDENT_ID can point to a different uniquely identified student.

phases.feedback: The foreign key must match the primary-key value in the other table.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how does a foreign key connect a payment to the correct student?
recall.empty_message: Write a short explanation before submitting.
recall.model_answer: The payment's foreign key stores a student ID. That value matches the unique primary key in Students, which identifies the related student row.

guidance.start_message: Trace the requested payment's foreign key to a Student row.

items.content: A foreign key value must match the primary-key value in the related table.

phases.title: Trace one relationship

phases.feedback: Find the same ID in the Students primary-key column.

guidance.start_message: Choose the requested record without being told the matching name.

items.content: PAYMENTS.STUDENT_ID points to STUDENTS.ID, not to the name directly.

phases.title: Identify the related record

phases.feedback: Read P003.STUDENT_ID, then look for the exact Students ID.

guidance.start_message: Solve a new foreign-key trace without hints.

target.label: TARGET

thinking.instruction: Before tracing visually, identify which references are valid and who the target payment belongs to.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not trace records yet. Match every foreign-key value mentally.

solve.title: Expert Key Relationships
solve.instruction: Trace the randomized target with no hints. Referential-integrity reasoning is the score.
solve.operation_rule: A foreign key is valid only when it matches an existing primary key.

solve.solved_result: The randomized relationship was traced correctly.
